holidays.name: National Cappuccino Day
holidays.description: A frothy salute to the espresso, steamed milk, and foam trio that has fueled mornings and fancy café dates for generations. Baristas everywhere are encouraged to flex their foam art skills.
holidays.origin: Cappuccino takes its name from the Capuchin friars, whose brown hooded robes resembled the drink's color. This unofficial food holiday is listed by food-day calendars and gained traction through coffee shops and social media.
holidays.funFact: In Italy, ordering a cappuccino after about 11 a.m. is considered a bit of a faux pas, since milky coffee is seen as a morning-only drink.

holidays.name: National Parfait Day
holidays.description: A day to celebrate the layered dessert, or breakfast in disguise, made of yogurt, fruit, granola, or ice cream stacked in a tall glass for maximum prettiness.
holidays.origin: The word parfait means perfect in French. The original French parfait was a frozen custard-style dessert, while the American version evolved into layered yogurt and ice cream cups.
holidays.funFact: A classic French parfait is not layered at all. It is a smooth, semi-frozen dessert made from egg yolks, sugar syrup, and whipped cream.

holidays.name: X-Ray Day (World Radiography Day)
holidays.description: A day to honor the mysterious rays that let us see our own bones without surgery. It celebrates radiographers and the science of seeing through things.
holidays.origin: On November 8, 1895, German physicist Wilhelm Conrad Röntgen discovered X-rays while experimenting with cathode ray tubes in his laboratory at the University of Würzburg.
holidays.funFact: Röntgen's first medical X-ray image was of his wife Anna Bertha's hand, complete with her wedding ring. She reportedly said, 'I have seen my death.'

holidays.name: Dunce Day
holidays.description: A day dedicated to the humble dunce cap and the legendary scholar behind it. People celebrate by embracing their inner goofball and making silly mistakes without shame.
holidays.origin: The day commemorates the birth of philosopher John Duns Scotus in 1266. His followers, the Dunsmen, were later mocked by critics, which turned his name into the word dunce.
holidays.funFact: Duns Scotus was actually one of the most brilliant medieval thinkers, and his name became an insult only after his ideas fell out of fashion.

holidays.name: Cook Something Bold and Pungent Day
holidays.description: A day to throw caution to the wind and fill your kitchen with big, aromatic flavors like garlic, onions, curry, and fermented foods. Bland is banned.
holidays.origin: This is a quirky unofficial food observance from fun-holiday calendars. It encourages home cooks to push past timid seasoning and experiment with strong flavors.
holidays.funFact: Garlic was reportedly fed to the workers who built the Egyptian pyramids, supposedly to keep them strong and healthy.
